implementerProof.how: Re-ran its command against tester-owned Postgres 17.11 and NATS 2.10.22 JetStream: LEGION_TEST_PG_DSN=postgres://legion@127.0.0.1:55532/postgres?sslmode=disable LEGION_TEST_NATS_URL=nats://127.0.0.1:4322 LEGION_TEST_NATS_MONITOR_URL=http://127.0.0.1:8322 go test -count=1 -run 'TestBlockedIssuesAreNotStartedAgainstScratchDispatch$' ./internal/daemon/ -v -> PASS in 15.01s; its new step answered the release out of backlog {"released":[-6,-7],"started":[],"held":[{"issue":-6,"blockedBy":[-2]}]} with the mirror held in share mode, and the unrecorded blocker's root was admitted 101.4ms after the close. The share-mode hold is the test's own (lock table dispatch_issues in share mode, to force the todo events after the answer); the product takes no lock, so I tested both orderings without it (releaseAnswer, below).

releaseAnswer.invariant: A child the answer calls held does not start until its blocker closes; a child it calls started is running a phase; an unblocked child is never called held; released is the whole request.
releaseAnswer.unforcedOrdering: Booted daemon, no hold on the mirror, five rounds in one tree with an open gate. Each round releases [A blocked by X, Dispatch backlog; B unblocked, backlog; C blocked by X, Dispatch already todo and held]. All five answered {released:[A,B,C], started:[], held:[A on X, C on X]}; once the events landed B reached planning, A and C stood at admitted named in admission.blocked on X. X closed in every round -> all ten held children reached planning, each with exactly one child-status 'every issue it waited on (X) is done'. PASS.
releaseAnswer.eventsForcedBeforeTheAnswer: Same scenario with a temporary 3s sleep inserted after the release's Dispatch writes (architect.go, before enterTodoChild and releaseOutcome; removed with jj restore afterwards), so every todo event lands before the answer is computed. All five answered {released:[A,B,C], started:[B], held:[A on X, C on X]}: the free child the release's own event started is named started, the blocked ones held, and the same settle and close checks pass. So the answer holds the invariant whichever way the race goes, not merely in the ordering one run happened to see: held is judged from the blockers Dispatch showed the request against the mirror (the judgement enterChild applies to the event that carries the same links), and started only from a record actually running a phase of a new run.
releaseAnswer.bite: The previous release answer (architect.go at 22bc5311) dropped into the head: round 0 answered held [C] only — the backlog child A, unrecorded when the answer was written, missing — and the scenario fails ('held = [{C [X]}]; want A and C held on X'). Restored with jj restore.
releaseAnswer.residual: The one window left is a blocker closing between the request's Dispatch read and its own todo write: the answer can then say held for a child whose todo event (published after that close) enters it with the blocker already done, so enterChild starts it directly — the child starts on its blocker's close, as held means, and its architect hears the ordinary phase-finished start rather than child-status. Not driven (sub-millisecond window); recorded so the reviewer can weigh it.
